claim: Let \(x\ge1\) be an integer, \(\tau>0\), \(\beta\ge0\), \(\delta\in\mathbb R\), and \(0<\alpha\le1\). A continuous-time simple symmetric nearest-neighbour walk on \(\{0,1,2,\ldots\}\), started at \(x\) and absorbed on hitting \(0\), has conditional Poisson jump rate \(\lambda_j\) during the \(j\)-th deterministic refresh interval of length \(\ell_j=\tau j^\beta[\log(ej)]^\delta\), where the \(\lambda_j\) are independent positive random variables with Laplace transform \(\mathbb E e^{-s\lambda_j}=(1+s^\alpha)^{-1}\) and are independent of jump directions. Write \(T\) for the absorption time, \(\gamma=(1+\alpha\beta)/[2\alpha(1+\beta)]\), and \(\eta=\delta(\gamma-1/2)\). Then, as \(t\to\infty\), \(\Pr(T>t)\sim C_{\alpha,\beta,\delta,\tau,x}\,t^{-\gamma}(\log t)^\eta\), with the explicit positive constant \(C_{\alpha,\beta,\delta,\tau,x}= [x\sqrt2\,\Gamma(1/(2\alpha))/(\alpha\pi)]\tau^{\gamma-1/2}(1+\alpha\beta)^{1/(2\alpha)}(1+\beta)^{-\gamma-\eta}\). Consequently for any \(q>0\), \(\mathbb E[T^q]<\infty\) exactly when \(q<\gamma\) or \(q=\gamma\) and \(\eta<-1\). In particular, \(\mathbb E[T]<\infty\) exactly when \(\alpha<1/(\beta+2)\), or \(\alpha=1/(\beta+2)\) and \(\delta<-2\).

correctness.rationale: The exact Poisson operational-time identity and reflected Bessel heat kernel give survival f_x(u)~x sqrt(2/pi) u^-1/2. The clock Laplace transform is a product of 1/(1+(s length)^alpha), and the maximal normalized alpha-weight vanishes for every beta>=0 and real delta, giving the positive alpha-stable operational-time limit. A Mellin–beta integral provides uniform negative q moments for q>1/2, justifying the unbounded inverse-square-root expectation. Karamata-type sum asymptotics and explicit logarithmic clock inversion give the displayed constant/exponents; tail integration gives the if-and-only-if q-moment criterion including eta<-1 at equality. Five exact rational exponent cases and four independently computed nonnegative spectral quadratures passed from the included executable path.

value.rationale: The result isolates a physically natural ageing mechanism absent from constant-relaxation-time analysis and gives an exact two-parameter first-passage and moment phase diagram. The sharp mean boundary moves from alpha=1/2 to alpha=1/(beta+2), and the logarithmic correction is decisive precisely at equality, including explicit opposite decisions for delta=-3 and delta=-2. The constant and full positive-moment frontier make this a substantive structural extension, rather than merely a simulation or relabeling.
